Delighted, Astra continued her work. She pulled silver threads from her tears of joy, crimson threads from her passion, and blue threads from her dreams. Each became a star, scattered across the cosmic tapestry.

But Astra grew lonely. She wove faster, creating countless stars, yet none could speak to her. In desperation, she wove one final thread—pulled from her very soul. This thread she shaped differently, weaving it into patterns of earth, water, and sky.

From this special thread, life emerged. And though Astra faded, becoming one with the darkness she had conquered, her creations remembered her. 

On clear nights, people gaze upward at the stars—the ancient weaver's handiwork—and tell stories, keeping Astra's memory alive through the very gift she gave them: the ability to create and share tales.
